# Language wrappers

What the dist layer owes a caller outside Rust. The one target that is BUILT
from this workspace is the C ABI, and it no longer lives under `wrappers/`:
it is [`dist/ffi`](../ffi/), the crate `sekejap-capi` with the lib name
`sekejap`, whose contract is [`docs/dist/C_ABI.md`](../../docs/dist/C_ABI.md)
and whose header is `dist/ffi/include/sekejap.h` — 59 `extern "C"` functions,
generated by cbindgen and committed. Every other target below binds that
header from its own toolchain; none of them is built by `cargo` here, and
none of them is tested by this workspace's test suite.

The 0.16 header was 41 functions addressed by a `"collection/key"` slug, with
`SekejapEngine*` as a second handle. 0.17 is addressed by collection and key
as two arguments, service mode is the same `SekejapDb*` opened another way,
and three symbols are kept as refusals. Which 0.16 symbol became which is
[`docs/dist/FFI_CONTRACT.md`](../../docs/dist/FFI_CONTRACT.md) §8; what every
wrapper therefore had to re-point is §8.1 and the table below.

| target | binds through | state at 0.17 |
|---|---|---|
| c | the ABI itself | nothing to re-point. `wrappers/c` is a README and examples over `dist/ffi/include/sekejap.h`; the library, the header and the packaging are in `dist/ffi` |
| csharp | P/Invoke, `Lib = "sekejap"` | PORTED, NOT BUILT HERE. All 59 functions (collection + key addressing, `SekejapScan`/`SekejapStatement`/`SekejapTx`, `SekejapStatus` on `SekejapException`). Written against the header but never compiled — this wrapper has not been built or run with `dotnet` yet — so there is no publish job for it in `release.yml` and there will not be one until a real `dotnet build` / `dotnet run` pass |
| dart | `dart:ffi` over the header | PORTED AND PUBLISHED. flutter_rust_bridge, the `dart/rust` glue crate and cargokit are gone; the package is pure Dart (`Db`, `Statement`, `Scan`, `Transaction`, one call per C function). `db_new` became `Db.openMemory()`, which keeps the name and refuses. `test-dart` and `publish-dart` in `release.yml` are un-gated; `publish-dart-generator` is gone with the typed-model generator |
| go | cgo `#include "sekejap.h"` | PORTED, PUBLISHED BY TAG. Every call site rewritten for collection + key, the 59-function surface wrapped one to one (`dist/bindings/wrappers/go/*.go`), `go test ./...` green against a prebuilt `libsekejap`. Go has no CI job to gate: a consumer resolves the module from a git tag, and the tag for it is **`dist/bindings/wrappers/go/v0.17.0`** — the module path is `github.com/sekejapdb/sekejap/dist/bindings/wrappers/go`, so Go's subdirectory-module convention prefixes the tag with that same path, not with `wrappers/go/` (`dist/bindings/wrappers/go/README.md` § Releases) |
| kotlin | JDK FFM downcalls (`Ffi.java`) | PORTED AND PUBLISHED on the desktop lane. All 59 functions, `SekejapStatus` beside the message, ONE artifact `life.sekejap:sekejap-ffm` for Java and Kotlin, tested against a built `libsekejap`. `publish-kotlin` in `release.yml` is un-gated. The 0.16 JNI lane (`rust/`, `orm/`, `sekejap-android/`) is removed, and `publish-kotlin-mobile.yml` is still `if: false`: Android has no `java.lang.foreign`, so that lane needs a JNI shim over this header before it can run |
| lua | a Lua C module over the header | PORTED, PUBLISHED BY HAND. Rewritten call sites, collection + key, `$n` parameters, scans, prepared statements, transactions, and a `GRAPH_TABLE` traversal test. There is no CI job for Lua at all; publishing is the procedure in `dist/bindings/wrappers/lua/README.md` § Publish |
| node | koffi over the header (was napi-rs over `CoreDB`) | PORTED AND PUBLISHED. The napi-rs Rust glue (`node/src/lib.rs`, its `Cargo.toml`, the committed `.node` binary and `node_modules/`) is gone; `wrappers/node/index.js` is pure JS, one `koffi.load()` of `libsekejap` at require time, all 59 C functions bound one to one (`wrappers/node/README.md`'s mapping table). `node-ffi-napi` was tried first and is unpublished from npm (404); koffi needs no native build. `build-node` and `publish-node` in `release.yml` are un-gated |
| python | ctypes over the header | PORTED AND PUBLISHED. `wrappers/python` is pure Python over the header; the PyO3 crate (`Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`) and the committed extension module are gone. A wheel carries `libsekejap` in `sekejap/_lib/`; the sdist carries none. `DB`/`Hit`/`EdgeHit` and the slug argument are replaced by `Db` and collection + key; `trim_memory`, `compact`, `show` and an in-memory open are refusals by name. `build-python-wheels`, `build-python-sdist` and `publish-python` in `release.yml` are un-gated |
| react-native | a JSI HostObject over the C ABI | **NOT PORTED AT 0.17, AND NOT PUBLISHED.** What is in `wrappers/react-native` is the 0.16 JSI scaffold: `cpp/sekejap-jsi.cpp` includes `../c/include/sekejap.h`, a path that no longer exists, and its README still shows the 0.16 typed-ORM API (`db.dishes.where(...).find()`), which is not a surface sekejap has. It has no release job, it is not on npm for 0.17, and nothing in this workspace builds or tests it. Porting it means rewriting the HostObject against `dist/ffi/include/sekejap.h` for collection + key addressing and rewriting the README against `docs/dist/C_ABI.md`; that work is not done here and the row is left saying so rather than implying otherwise |
| swift | a SwiftPM `systemLibrary` module map over the header | PORTED AND PUBLISHED. `Sekejap.swift` mirrors the 59 functions one to one, one class per handle (`Db`/`Statement`/`Scan`/`Tx`); `Sources/CSekejap/sekejap.h` is a symlink to `dist/ffi/include/sekejap.h`, so there is no vendored copy to drift; `Package.swift` runs no cargo command and links a prebuilt library through `$SEKEJAP_LIB_DIR`, falling back to `<repo root>/target/release`. `build-swift-xcframework` in `release.yml` is un-gated |

## What the release workflow actually does

`.github/workflows/release.yml` builds `libsekejap` from `dist/ffi` for five
desktop targets — linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-arm64, macos-x64,
windows-x64 — in `build-native-libs`, and attaches them plus the header in
`release-native-libs`. Every other job that publishes a wrapper is un-gated
and consumes those artifacts: `test-dart` / `publish-dart`,
`build-python-wheels` / `build-python-sdist` / `publish-python`,
`build-node` / `publish-node`, `publish-kotlin`, and
`build-swift-xcframework`.

Two jobs are gated, and each says why in the file:

- `publish-rust-cli` (`if: false`) — the CLI crate waits on the facade.
- `publish-kotlin-mobile.yml` (`if: false`) — Android needs a JNI shim,
  because it has no `java.lang.foreign`.

Three targets have no job at all and are published by hand or by tag: **go**
(a git tag, above), **lua** (its README's procedure), and **csharp** (which
has never been compiled). **react-native** has no job because it is not
ported.
